title: Bro Task Contract
$comment: The path patterns in $defs are the SAME language that bro_contracts.safe_repo_path / safe_work_path enforce procedurally. This schema is not decorative and not advisory: ContractSchemaAgreementTests in tests/test_bro_contracts.py runs one corpus of path strings through both this schema and those functions and fails if either accepts something the other rejects, and RealContractValidatesAgainstSchemaTests validates a runtime-accepted contract against this document. A change on one side must be mirrored on the other. Segment rule, used by every path form: no empty segment, no '.' or '..' segment, no leading/trailing whitespace in a segment, no backslash (refused outright rather than folded to '/', because a backslash is the classic way to smuggle a separator past a '..' rule), no ':' (drive letter, drive-relative 'C:x', Windows alternate data stream), no glob metacharacter '*?[' (M-6: a scope must be provably literal or the two enforcement layers disagree about what it covers), no NUL.

repoPath.$comment: A path relative to this checkout. '.' alone is the repository root entry itself and grants nothing beneath it. A leading '~' is refused: home-relative is not repo-relative.

absolutePath.$comment: A location named absolutely rather than relative to this checkout — the owner asked for specialists that can work in ordinary folders (a UI agent writing into a Desktop project), not only inside this repository. POSIX '/x' or Windows 'C:/x'; forward slashes only, so one pattern serves both. A bare filesystem root ('/' or 'C:/') is refused: that is not a scope, it is the absence of one. UNC and device namespaces ('//host/share', '\\?\C:\x') are refused because they bypass normal path resolution.

workPath.$comment: Where a task may act: a repo-relative path, or an absolute one. A scope entry is the ONLY place a specialist's reach is stated, so it is also the only place to read to know what one was allowed to touch. Syntax is all this can prove; real containment is decided at use time by bro_security.enforce_scope (which resolves symlinks and '..' before comparing) and by the operator-signed workspace binding, which remains the outer boundary an absolute scope entry cannot widen.
